title: Bayan Run 2026 Review: A Kalimantan Half Marathon from Indonesia's Coal Giant
seo_title: Bayan Run 2026 Review | Balikpapan Kalimantan Indonesia Race
meta_description: Bayan Run 2026: October 11 in Balikpapan, East Kalimantan. 21K to 800m kids from PT Bayan Resources — one of Indonesia's rarest race locations reviewed.
dek: Set for 11 October 2026 in Balikpapan, East Kalimantan, this PT Bayan Resources-organised run offers five distances. A coal-mining company's CSR road race in one of Indonesia's most remote race destinations — Kalimantan (Borneo).
verdict: Bayan Run 2026 is an outlier in Indonesian road racing — a multi-distance event in Balikpapan, East Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, where the running calendar is vanishingly thin. Organised by PT Bayan Resources, one of Indonesia's largest coal mining companies, as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) programme, the event offers five distances: 21K, 10K, 5K, 2.5K, and an 800m kids' run — a genuinely comprehensive range that covers competitive runners through to families. Balikpapan is East Kalimantan's largest city and a mining-industry hub, not a tourist destination, but it offers a rare access point to Kalimantan's interior. October in East Kalimantan is transitional — the dry season is winding down but conditions remain manageable. Registration is coming soon. For Indonesian runners seeking a genuinely rare race location — Kalimantan has perhaps the smallest running calendar of any major Indonesian island — or international runners wanting a Borneo race credit far from the beaten path, this is worth serious tracking.

sections.heading: Kalimantan: Indonesia's Racing Frontier
paragraphs: Kalimantan — the Indonesian portion of Borneo — is the least-represented major island on the Indonesian running calendar. [1] While Java, Sumatra, and even Sulawesi have established race circuits, Kalimantan's running scene is sparse: a handful of events in Balikpapan, Banjarmasin, and Pontianak, with long gaps between them. Bayan Run is one of the most prominent. For runners working through Indonesia's islands, Kalimantan is the hardest box to tick — and this race is the most accessible way to do it.

Balikpapan itself is a pragmatic city: built on oil and mining wealth, it has decent infrastructure by Kalimantan standards — an international airport (Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan), chain hotels, and good roads. [2] It's not a beauty destination, but it's a functional race base.

sections.heading: PT Bayan Resources: CSR with Scale
paragraphs: PT Bayan Resources is one of Indonesia's largest coal producers, and the Bayan Run is a CSR initiative — which, in the Indonesian corporate context, often means a well-resourced event funded by a company seeking to demonstrate community engagement. [1] The five-distance spread (21K down to 800m kids) is unusually comprehensive and suggests an organiser building for broad community participation rather than just competitive runners. The dual-venue setup — Lapangan Merdeka 3 and the BSCC Dome — indicates a substantial operational footprint. Corporate CSR races can be hit or miss in Indonesia, but the Bayan brand's resources suggest the logistics will be handled professionally.

sections.heading: October Climate: Kalimantan's Transitional Window
paragraphs: Indonesia's climate varies by region, and East Kalimantan sits close to the equator with a tropical rainforest climate. [3] October is transitional: the relatively drier period (June-September) is ending, but the heavier rains of November-December haven't fully arrived. Morning temperatures in Balikpapan are typically 24-26°C with high humidity throughout the year — this is equatorial Borneo, so don't expect cool conditions. Rainfall is possible at any time, but a morning race should see manageable conditions. [2]

sections.heading: The Five-Distance Spread
paragraphs: The distance options — 21K, 10K, 5K, 2.5K, and 800m kids — cover the full spectrum. [1] The 2.5K bridges the gap between the kids' run and the 5K for families running together. The 21K gives competitive runners a meaningful challenge. This is a race designed to bring an entire community out — consistent with CSR goals — rather than a niche competitive event. For visiting runners, the comprehensive race village atmosphere is part of the appeal.
